answer_text:
Partition the numbers into the 1004 pairs

\[
\{1,2008\},\{2,2007\},\dots,\{1004,1005\},
\]

each of which has sum \(2009\).

Let \(S\) be the chosen set of 1004 numbers. Since no two chosen numbers sum to \(2009\), \(S\) can contain at most one number from each pair. Because \(|S|=1004\), it must contain exactly one number from each pair.

Let \(T\) be the 1004 unchosen numbers. Then \(T\) also contains exactly one number from each pair.

The total sum of all numbers is

\[
1+2+\cdots+2008=\frac{2008\cdot 2009}{2}=2017036.
\]

So

\[
\sum_{t\in T} t=2017036-1009000=1008036.
\]

Thus

\[
\sum_{s\in S}s-\sum_{t\in T}t=1009000-1008036=964.
\]

Now let

\[
Q_S=\sum_{s\in S}s^2,\qquad Q_T=\sum_{t\in T}t^2.
\]

For each pair \(\{x,y\}\) with \(x+y=2009\),

\[
x^2-y^2=(x-y)(x+y)=2009(x-y).
\]

Summing over all pairs gives

\[
Q_S-Q_T=2009\left(\sum_{s\in S}s-\sum_{t\in T}t\right)
=2009\cdot 964=1936676.
\]

Also,

\[
Q_S+Q_T=1^2+2^2+\cdots+2008^2
=\frac{2008\cdot 2009\cdot 4017}{6}
=2700811204.
\]

Therefore,

\[
2Q_S=(Q_S+Q_T)+(Q_S-Q_T)
=2700811204+1936676=2702747880,
\]

so

\[
Q_S=\frac{2702747880}{2}=1351373940.
\]

\[
\boxed{1351373940}
\]
